disclaimer: This report is for educational and wellness purposes only. It is not a medical diagnosis and does not replace advice from a qualified healthcare professional. HbA1c results should be confirmed by your doctor. Do not start, stop or change any medication without medical advice.

status.label: In the normal range
status.explanation: Your HbA1c reflects average blood glucose over roughly the last 2–3 months and is below the 5.7% threshold used for prediabetes.

summary: Your HbA1c of 5.6 is in the normal range, which is a great sign for your overall health. Your BMI of 22.0 also falls in the normal category, and you don't have any major risk factors noted right now. To keep things this way, it helps to stay on top of routine checks like HbA1c and blood pressure, keep up your moderately active lifestyle, and continue following a balanced vegan, Mediterranean-style eating pattern with a calorie target around 1950 per day. These small, steady habits go a long way toward supporting your long-term wellness.

foods_to_eat: Whole grains like brown rice, quinoa, bulgur and whole wheat pasta
Legumes such as chickpeas, lentils and white beans
Plenty of non-starchy vegetables like zucchini, peppers, spinach and tomatoes
Healthy fats from olive oil, nuts, seeds and avocado
Soy-based products like soy milk, soy yogurt and tofu
Fresh fruit like berries, apples and figs in moderate portions
Herbs and spices such as oregano, mint, parsley and turmeric
foods_to_avoid: Sugary drinks and fruit juices with added sugar
Refined white bread, pastries and sweets
Deep-fried foods like fried falafel from takeaway shops
Processed meat substitutes high in sodium and additives
White rice and other highly refined grains in large portions
Packaged snacks high in salt and refined flour
plan.portion_guidance: Fill half your plate with non-starchy vegetables, one quarter with whole grains or starchy foods like quinoa or whole wheat pasta, and one quarter with a protein source like legumes or tofu. Use measures like a katori or small bowl for grains and legumes, and a cupped handful for nuts and seeds.
plan.hydration: Aim for about 8 to 10 glasses of water through the day. Herbal teas and infused water with lemon or mint are good options. Limit sugary drinks and sodas.

exercise: Continue at least 150 minutes a week of moderate activity, such as brisk walking, cycling, or swimming, spread across most days.
Add muscle-strengthening exercises on 2 days a week, such as bodyweight exercises, resistance bands, or light weights, allowing rest between sessions.
lifestyle.walking_goal: Aim for 30 minutes of brisk walking on at least 5 days a week. Since you are already moderately active, start with your current pace and gradually increase duration or intensity each week.
lifestyle.weight_management: Your BMI is in the normal range, so the focus should be on maintaining your current weight through balanced eating and regular activity rather than losing weight.
lifestyle.sleep: Aim for 7 to 9 hours of sleep each night. Try to keep a consistent bedtime and wake time, limit screens before bed, and create a cool, dark, quiet sleeping environment.
stress: Practice deep breathing or mindfulness meditation for 5 to 10 minutes daily to help manage everyday stress.
Schedule short breaks during your day for stretching or a brief walk outside to clear your mind.
behaviour_change: Keep up your current healthy habits around activity and avoiding tobacco, as this supports your long-term wellbeing.
Since you follow a vegan diet, consider periodically checking in with a healthcare provider to ensure you're getting enough vitamin B12, iron, and omega-3s.
Continue to avoid alcohol, as you already do, to support overall health.

monitoring.name: HbA1c
monitoring.why: Regular screening finds changes before symptoms appear.
monitoring.frequency: Every 3 years, or yearly if your doctor advises because of risk factors

monitoring.name: Blood pressure
monitoring.why: High blood pressure multiplies the heart and kidney risks of high blood glucose.
monitoring.frequency: At every doctor visit; at home regularly if you have high blood pressure

preventive_actions: Keep up regular physical activity most days of the week to support healthy blood sugar levels.
Continue eating a balanced, plant-based diet rich in vegetables, whole grains, and legumes.
Schedule routine HbA1c and blood pressure checks to catch any changes early.
Maintain your current healthy weight through consistent eating and activity habits.
Stay mindful of portion sizes to stay near your 1950 calorie target.

hba1c_caveat: HbA1c can be less accurate if you have anaemia, kidney disease, a recent blood transfusion or certain haemoglobin variants.
